stories.headline: Iran and Israel halt strikes at Trump's request after first fire exchange since April truce

key_facts.fact: Iran fired nearly 30 missiles at Israel; Israel struck military sites in Iran, marking the first exchanged strikes since a ceasefire began in early April
key_facts.excerpt: Iran fired nearly 30 missiles at Israel, according to the Israeli military, while Israel struck military sites in the Islamic republic.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters announced a halt to strikes, framing it as a 'completed operation' delivering a 'painful response' over Israeli strikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh district, while warning of 'far more intense and crushing' retaliation if Israel attacks again
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's military central command has announced a halt to its strikes against Israel, declaring it had delivered a 'painful response' to Israel over strikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh district -- but warned that any continuation of Israeli aggression would bring 'far more intense and crushing' retaliation.

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social that both sides were seeking an immediate ceasefire and said negotiators were in the 'final throes' of a Middle East peace deal; an Israeli official said Israel halted strikes on Iran at Trump's request
key_facts.excerpt: The White House confirmed that Trump had called Netanyahu to discuss the crisis. An Israeli official said Israel had halted its strikes at his request.

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu said 'fire is on hold' against Iran but warned that if Tehran 'make the mistake of resuming attacks against us, we will respond with full force'
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a short video released by his office on June 8 that 'fire is on hold' against Iran, after Tehran ended its attacks on Israel. But speaking for the first time after Iran launched missiles at Israel, he warned that should Tehran 'make the mistake of resuming attacks against us, we will respond with full force.'

key_facts.fact: Iran's initial attack on Sunday evening was retaliation for Israeli strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, which Tehran views as a violation of the US-Iran ceasefire that requires halting hostilities in Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Iran launched its first attack on Israel in several weeks on Sunday evening in retaliation for Israeli strikes on the southern suburbs of Lebanon's capital Beirut.

key_facts.fact: Despite the pause between Iran and Israel, Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 14 people on Monday, according to the Lebanese health ministry; Israel said offensive operations against Hezbollah would continue 'at full force'
key_facts.excerpt: But violence continued in southern Lebanon, where Israeli strikes killed at least 14 people on Monday, according to the Lebanese health ministry.

stories.headline: Iceye raises over €1B led by General Atlantic at €10B valuation as defense space demand surges

key_facts.fact: Iceye raised €450 million (USD 520 million) in a primary Series F round led by General Atlantic at a valuation of over €10 billion (over USD 12 billion); with a secondary placement the total transaction exceeds €1 billion
key_facts.excerpt: ICEYE, the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space, has raised EUR 450 million (USD 520 million) in a primary Series F funding round led by General Atlantic, at a valuation of over EUR 10 billion (over USD 12 billion). [...] Together with a secondary placement, the total fundraising round exceeds EUR 1 billion.

key_facts.fact: Additional investors include Solidium, Tesi, Varma, Ilmarinen, Lifeline Ventures, Nokia, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), and TCV
key_facts.excerpt: Additional investors include Solidium, Tesi, Varma, Ilmarinen, Lifeline Ventures, as well as Nokia, from Finland, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), and TCV.

key_facts.fact: Six months ago, in December 2025, Iceye was valued at €2.4 billion in a €150 million Series E led by General Catalyst, making the new round a more than fourfold valuation jump
key_facts.excerpt: In December 2025, ICEYE was valued at €2.4 billion. Today, it has closed a Series F round at over €10 billion.

key_facts.fact: The €450 million primary round is one of the largest single venture rounds for a European defence technology company; Iceye operates the world's largest SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) constellation
key_facts.excerpt: The €450 million primary round is one of the largest single venture rounds for a European defence technology company.

key_facts.fact: Iceye started as a climate monitoring business but has grown into a €10 billion company driven by higher defence spending in Europe and the Middle East; Poland recently signed a ~€200 million radar satellite deal, and the company is targeting €1 billion in revenue in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: We're less than a week out from the upcoming IPO of SpaceX, and today one of its big customers in Europe announced a huge funding round to boost its own growth. Iceye, the satellite startup from Finland that has made major inroads into national security, has closed just over €1 billion in growth funding led by General Atlantic with fellow Finnish company and industrial comms giant Nokia as an additional investor.

stories.headline: NinjaOne hits $12.3B valuation in $400M+ secondary; founders retain control of IT management platform

key_facts.fact: NinjaOne raised more than $400 million in Series C extensions at a $12.3 billion post-money valuation, more than doubling its $5 billion valuation from February 2025
key_facts.excerpt: NinjaOne raises more than $400 million in secondary funding at a $12.3 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: The Series C extension included Wellington Management, Teachers' Venture Growth, BDT & MSD Partners, Sequoia Capital, ICONIQ, Hedosophia, NEA, Washington Harbour Partners, CapitalG and Pinegrove Opportunity Partners
key_facts.excerpt: Series C extensions included investment from Wellington Management, Teachers' Venture Growth, BDT & MSD Partners, Sequoia Capital, ICONIQ, Hedosophia, NEA, Washington Harbour Partners, CapitalG, and Pinegrove Opportunity Partners

key_facts.fact: NinjaOne is now one of the most valuable VC-backed cybersecurity companies, surpassing Cyera, according to co-founder Chris Matarese
key_facts.excerpt: IT management platform NinjaOne raised more than $400 million at a $12.3 billion post-money valuation, co-founder Chris Matarese tells Axios Pro. Why it matters: NinjaOne is now one of the most valuable VC-backed cybersecurity companies, surpassing even Cyera.

key_facts.fact: The company posted ~70% year-over-year growth in 2025, achieved profitability in Q1 2026, and was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Management Tools
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement follows a landmark 2025 for NinjaOne that delivered nearly 70% year-over-year growth, along with a record-breaking first quarter, in which the company achieved profitability and was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Endpoint Management Tools.

key_facts.fact: NinjaOne remains founder-led and debt-free; co-founders Sal Sferlazza and Chris Matarese remain the largest equity holders and retain majority control of the board and voting power; the company has nearly 40,000 customers including Audi, Birkenstock, Carnival, Deloitte and Hyundai
key_facts.excerpt: NinjaOne remains founder-led and controlled. Co-founders Sal Sferlazza and Chris Matarese are still the largest equity holders in the company and have majority control of the Board of Directors and the company's voting power. NinjaOne has nearly 40,000 customers, including Arc'teryx, Audi Revolut F1 Team, Birkenstock, Carnival Cruise Line, Deloitte, Executech, GoFundMe, Hyundai...

stories.headline: Pentagon adds Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, Nio and dozens more to Chinese military companies list

key_facts.fact: On June 8 the US Department of Defense published an updated Section 1260H list designating Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, Nio, WuXi AppTec, Unitree, TP-Link, JA Solar, Trina Solar, CALB, EVE Energy, Hesai, RoboSense, BOE and CATL among more than 60 additions as 'Chinese military companies'
key_facts.excerpt: Among the most prominent additions were e-commerce giant Alibaba, search and AI company Baidu, electric vehicle manufacturers BYD and Nio, pharmaceutical research and manufacturing company WuXi AppTec, robot maker Unitree, networking equipment maker TP-Link and solar companies JA Solar and Trina Solar. The list also included battery makers CALB and EVE Energy, lidar firms Hesai and RoboSense, and display-panel manufacturer BOE Technology Group.

key_facts.fact: With these additions, the Pentagon has now declared all three of China's top AI champions (Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent) as supporting the People's Liberation Army; Tencent was added in 2025 and has been seeking removal
key_facts.excerpt: With the move, the US has now declared that three of China's artificial intelligence champions – Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent Holdings – aid the Asian country's armed forces. Tencent was added to the list in 2025 and has been seeking its removal.

key_facts.fact: Starting June 30, 2026, the FY 2024 National Defense Authorization Act will prohibit DoD from entering into or renewing direct contracts with listed entities; indirect-procurement restrictions take effect in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Starting June 30, the FY 2024 National Defense Authorization Act will prohibit DOD from entering into or renewing contracts for goods or services directly with listed entities. The same restrictions will apply to indirect goods or services starting a year from now.

key_facts.fact: The designation does not impose sanctions or block US trading but creates reputational and supply-chain risk; the list now includes more than 100 businesses, and an earlier version published briefly in February was withdrawn before being formally reissued
key_facts.excerpt: Those companies were on a previous update of the list that was posted briefly in February before being withdrawn minutes later. [...] First published in 2021, the 1260H list now includes more than 100 businesses accused of working with the Chinese military.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba called the designation baseless and said it would 'take all available legal action'; Baidu 'categorically' rejected the designation and WuXi AppTec called its listing 'incorrect'
key_facts.excerpt: Several other companies added to the list offerable similar pushback. Alibaba said there was 'no basis' for its inclusion; Baidu 'categorically' rejected the designation; WuXi AppTec called its listing 'incorrect'. Others, including BYD and battery makers CATL and Eve Energy, have yet to issue responses.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon's basis for Nio's designation cited direct and indirect SASAC affiliation and classification as a military-civil fusion contributor; for BYD, the basis was that the company operates within a military-civil fusion enterprise zone, without evidence of direct PLA contracting or technology transfer
key_facts.excerpt: For Nio, the filing cites direct and indirect affiliation with SASAC—China's state assets regulator—and classification as a military-civil fusion contributor linked to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. For BYD, the basis is that it operates within a military-civil fusion enterprise zone. Neither designation involves evidence of active military contracting, direct weapons supply or documented technology transfer to the People's Liberation Army.

stories.headline: Federal judge in Boston strikes down Trump's $100K H-1B visa fee as an unlawful tax

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston vacated Trump's $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa applications, ruling that the policy violated the federal Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution
key_facts.excerpt: A federal judge on Monday vacated President Donald Trump's $100,000 fee for employers' H-1B visa applications for highly-skilled foreign workers. The policy implementing the high fee on the visas for workers in a specialty occupation violated the federal Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution, Judge Leo Sorokin declared in the ruling in U.S. District Court in Boston.

key_facts.fact: Sorokin concluded the payment is functionally a tax that Congress had not delegated to the executive branch, writing 'the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called'
key_facts.excerpt: The Boston-based judge wrote 'the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called.'

key_facts.fact: The ruling came in a lawsuit filed by 20 Democratic state attorneys general; Trump implemented the fee via a presidential proclamation in September, arguing the H-1B program was being misused through 'large-scale replacement of American workers'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump implemented the $100,000 fee in a presidential proclamation last September. He argued that the H-1B visa program was being misused and undermining U.S. economic and national security through the 'large-scale replacement of American workers.'

key_facts.fact: The judge cited the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling striking down Trump's emergency-law tariffs, applying the same logic that the president lacks authority to levy a tax under immigration law
key_facts.excerpt: The judge cited the US Supreme Court's February ruling striking down Trump's sweeping tariffs he pursued under a law meant for use in national emergencies. Under the logic of the justices' decision in that case, Trump similarly had no authority under immigration law to levy a tax, Sorokin said.

key_facts.fact: The fee dramatically suppressed demand: as of February 15, US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received just 85 payments of the $100,000 fee, the administration disclosed in March filings
key_facts.excerpt: The increase in fees has discouraged H-1B visa requests, according to court filings. As of February 15, US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received just 85 payments of the $100,000 fee, the administration said in a March filing.

key_facts.fact: White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said the administration would appeal, noting that a federal judge in Washington DC had upheld a similar order in December
key_facts.excerpt: 'The H-1B program has been abused for decades, and President Trump finally took action to fix it. A federal judge in Washington already upheld a nearly identical order, and the Administration is confident this order will be reversed on appeal,' Rogers said.

stories.headline: FDA grants accelerated approval to Boehringer's zongertinib for HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval to zongertinib (Hernexeos), made by Boehringer Ingelheim, for adults with unresectable or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC whose tumors carry HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations detected by an FDA-authorized test
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA has granted accelerated approval to zongertinib (Hernexeos; Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) for adults with unresectable or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer(NSCLC) whose tumors have HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) activating mutations, as detected by an FDA-authorized test.

key_facts.fact: The decision expands the drug's August 2025 accelerated approval, which had been limited to HER2-mutant NSCLC patients who had already received prior systemic therapy
key_facts.excerpt: The decision expands upon the drug's August 2025 accelerated approval, which was granted for patients with HER2-mutant NSCLC who had received prior systemic therapy.

key_facts.fact: Regulatory support derived from Beamion LUNG-1 (NCT04886804), a single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multicohort trial of zongertinib in patients with HER2 gene changes
key_facts.excerpt: Regulatory support derives from Beamion LUNG-1, a single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multicohort design assessing [...] zongertinib [...] with HER2 gene changes.

key_facts.fact: The application was part of the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher pilot program, designed to accelerate review of products addressing national priorities
key_facts.excerpt: Its application was a part of the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher pilot program, which is designed to accelerate the review of products that can potentially address key national priorities.

sources.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to Zongertinib for HER2-Mutant NSCLC

stories.headline: Meta commits $115M to a free 5-week 'Workforce Academy' that guarantees data center construction jobs

key_facts.fact: Meta is launching a 'Workforce Academy', a $115 million free five-week program to train Americans to build its data centers, with participants guaranteed a job at one of Meta's construction sites
key_facts.excerpt: Five-week program, which is free of charge and guarantees a job, follows recent layoff of 8,000 employees

key_facts.fact: The initiative comes shortly after Meta cut about 8,000 employees and as the company ramps up massive AI data-center construction in the US
key_facts.excerpt: Five-week program, which is free of charge and guarantees a job, follows recent layoff of 8,000 employees

key_facts.fact: The program was announced via a Wall Street Journal op-ed co-authored by former Trump 45 alum Dina Powell McCormick and tradesman advocate Mike Rowe (mikeroweworks), framing it as tech and trades as 'interdependent, not rivals'
key_facts.excerpt: Great new initiative highlighted by @DinaPowellMcC & @mikeroweworks. Tech and trades are interdependent, not rivals. You can't build technological infrastructure without electricians, plumbers, techs...

sources.title: Meta Launches Workforce Academy to Train Workers to Build Data Centers
